newsitem.title: UK: GNI sticks to 180,000-tonne cocoa deficit forecast.
newsitem.headline: GNI sticks to 180,000-tonne cocoa deficit forecast.

text.p: Brokers GNI said the global cocoa deficit in 1996/97 was still likely to be closer to 180,000 tonnes despite the common view in the market that it may be no more than 100,000 tonnes.
"In our view there is still a greater probability of a deficit closer to 180,000 tonnes," GNI said in a montly commodity report.

It did not revise its production estimate from 2.559 million tonnes, although recent data from West Africa suggested an Ivorian crop of around one million tonnes and a Ghanaian crop of around 300,000-325,000, it said.
But a 50,000-tonne swing either way in the crop was still possible in Ivory Coast.
GNI had in January put the Ivorian and the Ghanaian harvests at 950,000 and 340,000 tonnes respectively.
In the latest report it said stocks were "more than ample" at present, and problems with the Ivorian midcrop was unlikely.

"So the market will have to wait until the results of the second quarter grind, and the preliminary indications for the 1997/98 main crop, before securing a fundamental reason to move prices higher," it added.
